title: 500 years of NOT teaching THE CUBIC FORMULA. What is it they think you can't handle?

timestamps.label: Opening: why isn't the cubic formula taught in school?
timestamps.note: Introduces the cubic formula and poses the central question: why do schools teach the quadratic formula but not the cubic?

timestamps.label: The simplified cubic x³ + px + q = 0 and its formula
timestamps.note: Pre-processing reduces any cubic to the depressed form x³ + px + q = 0; the resulting formula is much simpler than the general case.

timestamps.label: Historical context: Tartaglia, Cardano, and mathematical duels
timestamps.note: The cubic formula was kept secret for competitive advantage in 16th-century mathematical duels before Cardano published it.

timestamps.label: Completing the square: geometric derivation of the quadratic formula
timestamps.note: Geometric 'completing the square' is shown as a physical rearrangement of areas, deriving the quadratic formula from scratch.

timestamps.label: Parabola shift method: second derivation via turning point
timestamps.note: Shifting the parabola's turning point to the y-axis via calculus (derivative = 0) gives the −b/2a shift, cleanly deriving the formula.

timestamps.label: Cubic inflection point shift — pre-processing reduces to depressed cubic
timestamps.note: Shifting the cubic's inflection point to the y-axis using −b/3a eliminates the quadratic term, analogous to completing the square.

timestamps.label: Cubic discriminant (q/2)² + (p/3)³ determines number of solutions
timestamps.note: The sign of the cubic discriminant plays the same role as b²−4ac for quadratics: positive → 1 solution, negative → 3 solutions.

timestamps.label: Completing the cube: deriving Cardano's formula via u + v substitution
timestamps.note: Setting x = u + v and requiring uv = −p/3, the cubic reduces to a quadratic in u³, solved by the quadratic formula.

timestamps.label: Casus irreducibilis: three real roots require complex intermediate steps
timestamps.note: When the discriminant is negative (three real roots), Cardano's formula outputs complex numbers even though all solutions are real.

timestamps.label: Polar form and cube roots of complex numbers give all three solutions
timestamps.note: Writing complex cube-root expressions in polar form (r, θ) and dividing the angle by 3 recovers all three real solutions via trigonometry.

timestamps.label: Fun facts: tangent lines, equilateral triangles, and Marden's theorem
timestamps.note: Three geometric curiosities about cubics: tangent-line collinearity, equilateral triangle rotation to zeros, and Marden's theorem linking derivative zeros to an inscribed ellipse.

timestamps.label: Ferrari's quartic solution and the limits of radical formulas
timestamps.note: Ferrari's method solves the quartic; no quintic formula exists (proved by Galois theory) — there is no general solution in radicals beyond degree 4.

cross_domain.description: Casus irreducibilis forced Bombelli to invent complex numbers in the 16th century
cross_domain.note: The need to express real cubic roots through complex intermediates was the historical origin of complex number theory.

cross_domain.description: 16th-century mathematical duels: cubic formula kept secret as competitive weapon
cross_domain.note: Tartaglia and del Ferro withheld the cubic formula for use in public mathematical competitions before Cardano published it.

key_arguments: Any cubic ax³+bx²+cx+d can be reduced to the depressed form x³+px+q=0 by shifting x → x−b/3a (analogous to completing the square for quadratics).
The cubic discriminant Δ = (q/2)²+(p/3)³ determines the number of real solutions: Δ>0 → 1, Δ=0 → 2, Δ<0 → 3.
Cardano's formula solves the depressed cubic via x=u+v with uv=−p/3, reducing the problem to a quadratic in u³.
The casus irreducibilis: when Δ<0 (three real roots), the formula necessarily passes through complex numbers — this paradox historically drove the invention of complex numbers.
Complex cube roots in polar form (r·e^{iθ}) yield all three real solutions via cos(θ/3+2πk/3); Galois theory proves no purely real radical formula exists for this case.
